record.paper_title: Five open problems in theory of quantum information
record.original_question: Determine whether all negative-partial-transpose entangled states represent quantum privacy that can be distilled to private bit states, and, if the answer is positive, determine whether such private-bit distillation can be achieved with one-way classical communication from one party to the other. Here negative partial transpose means the partial transpose of the bipartite density matrix has a strictly negative eigenvalue, and private bit states are the target privacy resource.

evidence.quote: Otherwise, if some eigenvalues of ρΓ are strictly smaller than zero, the state has negative partial transpose (NPT).

Problem 4 seems to be rather complex, so its solution may involve some novel techniques concerning tensor products of several matrices. Its positive solution would likely stimulate research on an important question relevant for quantum communication, namely, whether all NPT entangled states represent quantum privacy that may be distilled to the so-called private bit states – see [144]. If the answer were positive, the practical question would be, whether such a distillation procedure can be achieved in the scheme called ‘one-way classical communication’, in which one party, say Alice, communicates classical bits to Bob, and not vice versa.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\rho_{AB}$ be a bipartite density matrix on a finite-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_A\otimes\mathcal{H}_B$. The partial transpose $\rho_{AB}^{\Gamma}$ (taken on system $B$) is defined by $\langle i,k|\rho^{\Gamma}|j,l\rangle = \langle i,l|\rho|j,k\rangle$. The state $\rho_{AB}$ is said to have negative partial transpose (NPT) if $\rho_{AB}^{\Gamma}$ has at least one strictly negative eigenvalue, and is called NPT entangled when it is also entangled (which, for NPT states, follows automatically by the Peres criterion).

A private bit (pbit) is a bipartite state of the form
$$\gamma_{AA'BB'} = U\bigl(|\Phi^+\rangle\langle\Phi^+|_{AB}\otimes\sigma_{A'B'}\bigr)U^\dagger,$$
where $|\Phi^+\rangle = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}(|00\rangle+|11\rangle)$ is the two-qubit maximally entangled state held jointly by Alice ($A$) and Bob ($B$), $\sigma_{A'B'}$ is an arbitrary state of the auxiliary "shield" systems $A'$ (held by Alice) and $B'$ (held by Bob), and $U$ is a "twisting" unitary of the form $U = \sum_{ij}|ij\rangle\langle ij|_{AB}\otimes U_{ij}^{A'B'}$ with each $U_{ij}^{A'B'}$ unitary on $A'B'$. Measuring $A$ and $B$ in the computational basis of a pbit yields a perfectly correlated and uniformly random bit that is decoupled from any purifying eavesdropper, hence the term "private bit."

Distillability of pbits is defined under the class of LOCC (local operations and classical communication): $\rho_{AB}$ is said to allow pbit distillation if for every $\epsilon>0$ and some integer $m\ge 1$ there exists an LOCC protocol mapping $\rho_{AB}^{\otimes n}$ (for some $n$) to a state $\tau$ on $AA'BB'$ with $\|\tau - \gamma_m\|_1 \le \epsilon$ for some $m$-pbit $\gamma_m$, and the asymptotic key rate is positive. The protocol is called one-way (from Alice to Bob) if all classical messages exchanged during the LOCC flow only from Alice to Bob.

Determine the truth of the following statements.

(a) Every NPT entangled bipartite state $\rho_{AB}$ admits a pbit-distillation protocol with positive asymptotic key rate.

(b) If (a) holds, then for every NPT entangled $\rho_{AB}$ such a pbit-distillation protocol can be implemented using only one-way classical communication from Alice to Bob.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether all NPT entangled states are distillable (in particular to private-bit form) is a long-standing open problem in quantum information theory, closely tied to the conjectured existence of NPT bound entanglement for Werner states. Recent works (e.g., 2024 articles on the NPT bound problem and on bipartite bound entanglement) explicitly describe it as still unresolved, with only partial progress.

status_evidence.title: Unveiling NPT bound problem: From Distillability Sets to Inequalities and Multivariable Insights
status_evidence.snippet: The existence of NPT bound entanglement is an important open problem in quantum information theory.
status_evidence.claim: The NPT distillability question remains open as of 2024.

status_evidence.title: BIPARTITE BOUND ENTANGLEMENT
status_evidence.snippet: Equivalence between PPT entanglement and bound entanglement is a long-standing open problem; limited progress has been made even on Werner states.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture that NPT entangled states are distillable is unresolved.

status_evidence.title: A few steps more towards NPT bound entanglement
status_evidence.snippet: Steps towards proving existence of NPT bound entangled states.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial progress has been achieved on the distillability of NPT states.
